page.layout: One column of italic text, filling the page. At the bottom right, below the last line, the catchword.

p.i: Theologiam sponte sua et quasi natali genio multo propensiorem esse animum meum, quàm ad illam rixosam Controversiarium. Cum itaque mihi nunc aliquid esset necessario et subito faciendum, nec quaspiraret favoris vestri aura in hac tanta temporis angustia satis explorare possem: obsecutus ingenio meo, ad Moralem Theologium inflexi cursum. Cumque cogitarem quam sit grave Perjurii peccatum Deo pariter & hominibus exosum; simulque animadvertercm quot hominum myriades his perturbatissimis temporibus tàm nefario crimine se implicuerint, dum aut vobis metu adasti, aut inducti[?] dolo, juramentis se obstrinxerunt variis, et interdum, sic inter se adversis, ut alterutrum sine certa perjurii periculo nec suscipi potuerit, nec præstari: ex-

page.notes: Stains at the lower left are not printed text and are left out. "Controversiarium" is printed "Controversarium" with a line-end hyphen, so it is written with the hyphen as "Contro-versiarium" in the text above; "inducti" is uncertain (the letters after "ind" are hard to make out), and "adasti" is read as printed. The final word "ex-" ends the page with a printed hyphen; the catchword "istimavi" is partly cut off at its beginning, so the initial letter may be lost.
